_readme: s1116: per-report title, meta and lead for /r/<slug>/ pages Google shows for a named query. Read by site/src/data/rOverrides.ts. Facts come from the slug's row in data/readiness-servers.json (check of 2 Nov 2026); product claims are attributed to the registry entry. related = other /r/ slugs.

io-stackcut-stackcut.title: Stackcut (stackcut.io) MCP server: 24 tools, no sign-in
io-stackcut-stackcut.description: Stackcut's remote MCP server at stackcut.io/mcp helps cancel or cut subscriptions. On 2 Nov 2026 it needed no sign-in, listed 24 tools and scored 98 (A).
io-stackcut-stackcut.lead: Stackcut (stackcut.io) runs a remote MCP server at https://stackcut.io/mcp. Its registry entry says it helps you cancel or cut any subscription, with exit steps, cheaper plans, alternatives and the cheapest stack. When we checked it on 2 November 2026 it asked for no sign-in, listed 24 tools and scored 98 of 100 (grade A).

ai-elaichi-mcp.title: Elaichi AI vs running your own MCP servers
ai-elaichi-mcp.description: What Elaichi AI's MCP server is, from its registry entry and our 2 Nov 2026 check (OAuth sign-in, grade B), and what running your own MCP servers takes instead.
ai-elaichi-mcp.lead: Elaichi AI (elaichi.ai) describes itself in the MCP Registry as governed AI agents for the software your company already runs, with 400+ connectors behind one endpoint. You connect one hosted URL, https://api.elaichi.ai/mcp, and sign in with OAuth; its tools sit behind that sign-in, so our check without credentials could not list them. Running your own MCP servers instead means you host, secure and update each server yourself. [Run your own MCP stack](/run-your-own-mcp-stack/?src=r-elaichi) covers the architecture, a security checklist and the monthly cost.

ai-smithery-docfork-mcp.title: Docfork MCP server: library docs for AI code editors
ai-smithery-docfork-mcp.description: Docfork's MCP server on Smithery gives LLMs and AI code editors the latest docs and code examples for libraries. OAuth sign-in; grade B (85) on 2 Nov 2026.
ai-smithery-docfork-mcp.lead: Docfork serves the latest documentation and code examples for 9,000+ libraries to LLMs and AI code editors, according to its registry entry. This report covers the Smithery-hosted endpoint, https://server.smithery.ai/@docfork/mcp/mcp, which asks for an OAuth sign-in; the source is at github.com/docfork/docfork-mcp. On 2 November 2026 it scored 85 of 100 (grade B), and the Gemini sign-in discovery check failed (details below).

ai-sellerforge-sellerforge.lead: SellerForge (sellerforge.ai) connects Amazon Seller Central and Amazon Ads data to AI clients: account health, FBA inventory, reimbursements and keywords, per its registry entry. io-scanbimlabs-twinmotion.title: Twinmotion MCP server and Claude: what our check found
io-scanbimlabs-twinmotion.description: ScanBIM Labs' Twinmotion MCP server (rendering and video export via Datasmith) answered HTTP 401 with no OAuth discovery on 2 Nov 2026. Grade F, 39 of 100.
io-scanbimlabs-twinmotion.lead: ScanBIM Labs publishes a Twinmotion MCP server at https://mcp.scanbimlabs.io/twinmotion for rendering and video export through the Datasmith pipeline, per its registry entry. On 2 November 2026 it answered HTTP 401 without a WWW-Authenticate header or OAuth discovery documents, so our check could not start a sign-in or list its tools. Before you add it to Claude or another client, read the setup notes in its repo, github.com/ScanBIM-Labs/twinmotion-mcp.
